narrator: Jonathan Harker, Dr. Seward, Mina Harker
summary: After Renfield's scene the party goes to Carfax at dawn. Godalming brings a silver dog whistle; Van Helsing equips each man with a silver crucifix, garlic wreath, revolver, knife, electric lamp and a piece of Sacred Wafer. Seward picks the lock with skeleton keys. In the chapel only twenty-nine of fifty earth boxes remain; the vault is thick with a foul odour and swarms with thousands of rats, which Godalming's three terriers drive off once carried over the threshold. The party finds nothing else and locks up. Van Helsing notes the Count's animals fear dogs. Twenty-one boxes are now accounted for as removed. Van Helsing is rebuffed by Renfield. Mina, kept in the dark, dreams of mist pouring in with red eyes and a livid face, and on 2 October takes a mild sleeping draught from Seward.

scenes.title: Silence after Renfield
scenes.summary: The men debate whether Renfield was sane; Van Helsing chooses caution. Godalming fetches the silver whistle.
scenes.key_quote: That old place may be full of rats, and if so, I’ve got an antidote on call.

scenes.title: Arming on the porch
scenes.summary: Van Helsing lays out four sets of weapons and wards and distributes them.
scenes.key_quote: we need arms of many kinds. Our enemy is not merely spiritual.

scenes.title: Opening the door
scenes.summary: Seward finds a skeleton key; rusty bolt clangs back. The party enters, Van Helsing crossing himself and saying 'In manus tuas, Domine!'. Dust shows hobnail prints and a table with a bunch of labelled keys.
scenes.key_quote: “In manus tuas, Domine!” he said, crossing himself as he passed over the threshold.

scenes.title: The chapel and the stench
scenes.summary: Using Jonathan's map they find the iron-banded oak door; the foul air; only twenty-nine of fifty boxes remain. Godalming thinks he sees the Count's face in the passage, but it is shadows.
scenes.key_quote: it seemed as though corruption had become itself corrupt.

scenes.title: The rats and the terriers
scenes.location: Chapel and its outer iron-bound oaken door
scenes.summary: A phosphorescent mass of rats swarms. Godalming opens the outer door and blows the silver whistle; terriers come but halt howling at the threshold until carried in, then kill rats until the horde vanishes.
scenes.key_quote: the place made look like a bank of earth set with fireflies.

scenes.title: Withdrawal at dawn
scenes.summary: The house is searched; nothing more. Van Helsing locks the hall door and keeps the key, observing that rats flee from small dogs.
scenes.key_quote: we have reason to be content with our first night’s work.

scenes.title: Van Helsing visits Renfield
scenes.summary: Renfield sullenly insults Van Helsing and falls silent.
scenes.key_quote: you are the old fool Van Helsing.

scenes.title: Mina's mist dream
scenes.summary: Mist creeps across the lawn and pours through the door joins; a pillar of cloud with two red eyes forms and a livid white face bends over her.
scenes.key_quote: The last conscious effort which imagination made was to show me a livid white face bending over me out of the mist.

scenes.title: Mina takes a sleeping draught
scenes.summary: Renfield kisses her hand and blesses her in the afternoon; Seward gives her a mild sleeping draught.

locations.quote: The floor was seemingly inches deep, except where there were recent footsteps

locations.description: Reached through a low arched oaken door ribbed with iron bands; small, close, foul; holds the earth chests; vaulted door to a dark passage with solid walls and no hiding place.
features: arched oak door with iron bands
outer iron-bound oaken door with huge bolts and lock
locations.quote: a low, arched oaken door, ribbed with iron bands.

locations.name: Seward's lawn and mist
locations.description: Lawn where a white mist creeps toward the house against the walls.
locations.quote: a thin streak of white mist, that crept with almost imperceptible slowness across the grass towards the house

locations.name: Mina's bedroom

locations.atmosphere: dank and cold in the dream
locations.quote: The gaslight which I had left lit for Jonathan, but turned down, came only like a tiny red spark through the fog

creatures.name: Rats of Carfax
creatures.description: Thousands of rats with glittering baleful eyes, bodies dark, eyes shining like fireflies in lamplight.
creatures.behaviour: Appear from corners in a phosphorescent swarm and multiply by the minute; summoned by the Count.
weaknesses: not under the Count's spiritual power once dogs attack
creatures.quote: The rats were multiplying in thousands, and we moved out.

creatures.name: Terriers (3)
creatures.description: Dogs of Lord Godalming that howl at the chapel threshold but fight when placed inside.
creatures.behaviour: Kill rats by the score; frisk around once the evil leaves.
weaknesses: fear the threshold until carried in
creatures.quote: The instant his feet touched the ground he seemed to recover his courage

creatures.name: Mist (Count in dream)
creatures.description: White mist entering through door joins forming a pillar with two red eyes.
creatures.quote: a sort of pillar of cloud in the room

creatures.name: Shadow face illusion
creatures.description: A glimpse of the Count's face in the dark passage, pale with red eyes and lips.
creatures.quote: the high lights of the Count’s evil face, the ridge of the nose, the red eyes, the red lips, the awful pallor.

vampire_lore.rule: Animals obey him but are not immune to ordinary foes
vampire_lore.detail: Rats flee from small dogs; his spiritual power does not shield them.
vampire_lore.quote: the brute beasts which are to the Count’s command are yet themselves not amenable to his spiritual power

vampire_lore.rule: Count can handle earth boxes himself
vampire_lore.detail: (Chapter 20 confirms); here boxes were taken out by the door where dust was disturbed.
vampire_lore.quote: the boxes which had been taken out had been brought this way.

vampire_lore.detail: Mist enters via the door joins; Mina's dream foreshadows his access.
vampire_lore.quote: pouring in, not through the window, but through the joinings of the door.

vampire_lore.detail: The stench of the Count's resting place is unbearable.
Two red eyes in the mist.
vampire_lore.quote: the fire divided, and seemed to shine on me through the fog like two red eyes

puzzles.name: Lock and key
puzzles.setup: Locked hall door and chapel door.
puzzles.obstacle: Must enter without breaking the house.
puzzles.book_solution: Seward tries skeleton keys until the bolt yields; Jonathan finds the chapel key on the bunch on the hall table.
puzzles.game_idea: Lockpick minigame plus key-matching using the label hints and the map.
puzzles.quote: After a little play back and forward the bolt yielded, and, with a rusty clang, shot back.

puzzles.name: Find the way to the chapel
puzzles.setup: Dark dusty house with wrong turnings.
puzzles.book_solution: Jonathan recalls the layout and checks the map.
puzzles.game_idea: Maze navigation with a map and lamp.
puzzles.quote: after a few wrong turnings found myself opposite a low, arched oaken door

puzzles.name: Count the boxes
puzzles.obstacle: Finding how many are gone and where they went.
puzzles.book_solution: Count 29 left; disturbed dust shows route out of the outer door.
puzzles.game_idea: Footprint-and-dust trail reading to deduce which boxes left and how.
puzzles.quote: the dust had been much disturbed: the boxes which had been taken out had been brought this way.

puzzles.name: Rat swarm
puzzles.setup: Thousands of rats in the chapel.
puzzles.obstacle: Dogs refuse to cross the threshold.
puzzles.book_solution: Carry each dog in so its feet touch the floor.
puzzles.game_idea: Environmental puzzle: open the outer door, call dogs, and place them inside.
puzzles.quote: Lord Godalming lifted one of the dogs, and carrying him in, placed him on the floor.

combat.name: Rat swarm in the chapel
combat.tactics: Retreat, open the door, summon dogs, lift them over the threshold to attack.
combat.game_idea: Swarm encounter with morale: players must use the dogs as summons; swarm size grows each turn until countered.
combat.quote: They fled before him so fast that before he had shaken the life out of a score, the other dogs, who had by now been lifted in the same manner, had but small prey
